title: Benchmark Proposal: Ground-Truth Circuits from Procedurally Generated Algorithmic Tasks

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong: a scalable benchmark for circuit recovery is foundational infrastructure that would enable the entire field to measure progress. Addresses an identified top priority in the Open Problems paper.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: designing a procedural task generator from compositional algorithm specifications requires strong software engineering and algorithm design skills. Validating against three circuit discovery methods adds further expertise requirements.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Very ambitious: building a generator, training models on generated tasks, validating against three methods, and packaging as an open benchmark. This is a multi-month project, not a 30-hour sprint.

novelty.reasoning: MIB provides a mechanistic interpretability benchmark with ground-truth evaluation tracks, and Tracr provides compiled ground-truth circuits. However, neither offers a procedural generator that creates arbitrary compositional tasks with known ground-truth circuits at scale. The procedural generation aspect is novel, but the benchmark infrastructure space is becoming crowded, reducing the marginal contribution.

evidence.finding: Establishes two evaluation tracks — circuit localization and causal variable localization — across diverse tasks (IOI, arithmetic, MCQA, ARC) and models, with faithfulness integral, minimality, and AUROC metrics.

evidence.source: Tracr: Compiled Transformer Circuits (Lindner et al., 2024)
evidence.finding: Compiles RASP programs into actual Transformer weights, providing ground-truth circuits for algorithmic tasks, but limited to a specific programming model.
Evaluates across 62 algorithmic tasks, complementary to GPT-4; enables discovery of finite-state procedures without human-generated training data.
